---
title: "Noise Reduction"
description: "Turn down steady background noise such as hiss, hum and fans, under speech as well as between words, with no noise sample needed."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Noise Reduction turns down steady background noise such as hiss, hum and fan noise. It works out the noise level from the clip itself, so you don't need to give it a sample of the noise or a stretch of silence.

<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Noise Reduction" tools="set_audio" />

## Remove noise

<Steps>

1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **Noise Reduction** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).

2. Raise **Remove noise** while you listen, until the noise is low enough and the voice still sounds natural.

</Steps>

| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Remove noise** | How much steady background noise to remove. Quick values: 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 %. | 0 to 100 % | 0 % (off) |
| **Depth** | Read-only. See [The Depth read-out](#the-depth-read-out). | | off |

**Reset** in the section's header sets **Remove noise** back to 0.

## The Depth read-out

**Depth** tells you the most any part of the sound can be turned down at this setting. It follows **Remove noise**:

| Remove noise | Depth reads |
| --- | --- |
| 0 % | off |
| 25 % | 2 dB at most |
| 50 % | 6 dB at most |
| 75 % | 12 dB at most |
| 100 % | floor removed |

Noise Reduction never removes more than the noise level it found, so a higher setting isn't a stronger cut across the whole sound.

## What it can't do

Noise Reduction isn't a gate. It works under speech as well as between words, and it doesn't silence the gaps. To turn the pauses down, use the [Gate](/audio/gate/).

It can't remove a sound that isn't steady, such as a door slam or a cough. A long held note may eventually be treated as noise.

To remove music or voices in the background, or the echo of a room, use [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/). The two work together: Noise Reduction then works on the isolated sound.

## Good to know

- It runs after the EQ and [hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/), and before the [Gate](/audio/gate/) and the [Compressor](/audio/compressor/). See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).
- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, **Remove noise** writes the action's end and the amount glides across the action.
- Noise Reduction set on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip has no effect. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.

## Related

- [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/)
- [Hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/)
- [Gate](/audio/gate/)
- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/)

---
title: "Hum removal"
description: "Notch out mains hum at 50 or 60 Hz and its harmonics, and leave the voice between them alone."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Hum removal cuts the low electrical hum that mains power can leave on a recording. It places a narrow notch at the mains frequency and at each of its multiples, and leaves the sound between the notches alone.

<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Hum" tools="set_audio" />

## Remove hum

<Steps>

1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **Hum** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).

2. Tick **Remove hum**. It starts at 60 Hz, 30 dB deep, with 4 harmonics.

3. Set **Mains** to the frequency where the recording was made.

4. If you can still hear the hum, raise **Depth** or **Harmonics**.

</Steps>

The other controls are dimmed until **Remove hum** is ticked. **Reset** in the section's header turns hum removal off.

## The controls

| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Remove hum** | Turns hum removal on. | On or off | Off |
| **Mains** | The mains frequency where the recording was made: 50 Hz in most of the world, 60 Hz in the Americas and parts of Asia. | 50 Hz or 60 Hz | 60 Hz |
| **Depth** | How far each notch turns the hum down. Quick values: 12, 24, 30 and 48 dB. | 6 to 60 dB | 30 dB |
| **Harmonics** | How many notches: the mains frequency and its multiples. Quick values: 1, 2, 4 and 8. | 1 to 8 | 4 |

At 60 Hz with 4 harmonics, the notches sit at 60, 120, 180 and 240 Hz.

Each notch is about a tenth of the mains frequency wide, whatever its depth, so a notch at 60 Hz is about 6 Hz wide.

## Good to know

- Hum removal runs after the [EQ](/audio/eq/). Its notches appear in the EQ section's drawn curve, but the EQ's **Bypass** doesn't turn them off.
- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, these controls write the action's end. **Depth** glides across the action. **Mains**, **Harmonics** and turning hum removal on or off change at the action's end, with no glide.
- Hum removal set on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip has no effect. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.

## Related

- [EQ](/audio/eq/)
- [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/)
- [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/)

---
title: "Gate"
description: "Turn a clip down in the pauses between phrases, so room noise and breaths get quieter while the speech stays as it is."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The gate turns a clip down in its pauses. When the sound falls below the threshold it's pushed further down, so room noise and breaths between phrases get quieter while the speech itself is untouched.

<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Gate" tools="set_audio" />

<Shot
  name="09c-clip-sound-dynamics.inspector"
  alt="The Gate section of the Sound tab with Gate pauses ticked: Threshold −10 dB, Ratio 4.0:1, Range 20 dB, Attack 1 ms, Hold 50 ms, Release 100 ms, Status reading Opens above −31.8 dBFS, and Loudness −21.8 LUFS."
/>

## Gate the pauses

<Steps>

1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **Gate** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).

2. Tick **Gate pauses**. It starts at the [defaults](#the-controls), which work from the clip's own loudness.

3. Play the clip. If the ends of words are being cut, raise **Hold** or lower **Threshold**.

4. If the pauses aren't quiet enough, raise **Range**. If they sound too empty, lower it.

</Steps>

The other controls are dimmed until **Gate pauses** is ticked. **Reset** in the section's header turns the gate off.

## The controls

| Control | What it does | Range | Default | Quick values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Threshold** | How far under the clip's loudness the gate opens. | −40 to 0 dB | −10 dB | −20, −15, −10, −6 |
| **Ratio** | How strongly sound under the threshold is turned down. At 4:1, each dB under the threshold becomes 3 dB further down. | 1:1 to 20:1 | 4:1 | 2, 4, 10, 20 |
| **Range** | The most the gate ever takes away. | 1 to 80 dB | 20 dB | 10, 20, 40, 80 |
| **Attack** | How quickly it opens when the sound rises. | 0 to 100 ms | 1 ms | 1, 5, 10 |
| **Hold** | How long it stays open after the sound falls, so the ends of words aren't clipped. | 0 to 500 ms | 50 ms | 0, 50, 100, 200 |
| **Release** | How quickly it closes after the hold. | 1 to 2,000 ms | 100 ms | 50, 100, 250, 500 |

## The threshold follows the clip

**Threshold** is set in dB under the clip's own loudness, not at a fixed level, so the same setting works on a quiet recording and a loud one. A trim, a pan change or a different channel choice moves the loudness, and the threshold moves with it.

That loudness is the Loudness figure in the [Volume](/audio/volume/) section. It's measured before noise reduction, the compressor, the volume, the fades and ducking, so moving the Volume slider doesn't change where the gate opens.

## Read Status and Loudness

Two read-outs at the foot of the section show what the threshold means for this clip. With several clips selected, both read "—".

**Loudness** is the level the threshold is measured from, for example "−21.8 LUFS". It reads "measuring…" until the clip has been measured.

**Status** says where the gate opens, or why it isn't working:

| Status | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| off | **Gate pauses** isn't ticked. |
| Opens above −31.8 dBFS | The clip's loudness plus the **Threshold**. Here, −21.8 LUFS with a −10 dB threshold. |
| Waits for its loudness | The clip hasn't been measured yet. See below. |
| Not gating: too short | The clip plays for under 0.4 s, too short to measure. |
| Not gating: too quiet | The clip is too quiet to measure. |
| Not gating: no sound | The clip plays no sound in this timeline, or it's a nest clip. |

## Before the clip's loudness is measured

The gate, the [leveller](/audio/leveller/) and the [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/) all depend on the clip's measured loudness. Until it lands, the clip plays without them, and the preview picks them up by itself.

An export waits until every gated, levelled or de-essed clip has been measured. After five minutes without a measurement it stops, saying that the clip's loudness or speech hasn't been measured yet, and to wait for the Status rows to show the clip's loudness and export again.

A clip that can't be measured, because it's under 0.4 s or too quiet, plays and exports without them, and the export doesn't wait for it.

## Good to know

- The gate runs after [noise reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/) and before the leveller, the de-esser and the [compressor](/audio/compressor/). See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).
- The gate doesn't look ahead, so a loud start after a long pause can lose its first millisecond while the gate opens.
- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, these controls write the action's end. The numbers glide across the action, and turning the gate on or off changes at the action's end.
- The gate does nothing on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.

## Related

- [Leveller](/audio/leveller/)
- [De-esser](/audio/de-esser/)
- [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/)
- [Compressor](/audio/compressor/)

---
title: "De-esser"
description: "Tame the hard s, sh and t sounds a close microphone exaggerates, turning down only the top of the voice while they last."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The de-esser tames sibilance, the hard "s", "sh" and "t" sounds a close microphone exaggerates. It listens to the sound above its frequency and turns only that band down while it's over the threshold, so the rest of the voice keeps its level.

<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ De-esser" tools="set_audio" />

## Reduce sibilance

<Steps>

1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **De-esser** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).

2. Tick **Reduce sibilance**. It starts at 6,000 Hz, a threshold of 0 dB and a range of 6 dB.

3. Play a part with hard "s" sounds. If they're still sharp, lower **Threshold** or raise **Range**.

4. If the voice sounds dull or lisped, raise **Threshold** or lower **Range**. Move **Frequency** to where the sibilance sits in this voice.

</Steps>

The other controls are dimmed until **Reduce sibilance** is ticked. **Reset** in the section's header turns the de-esser off.

## The controls

| Control | What it does | Range | Default | Quick values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Frequency** | Where the sibilant band starts. | 2,000 to 12,000 Hz | 6,000 Hz | 4,000, 5,000, 6,000, 8,000 |
| **Threshold** | How loud the band must get, relative to the clip's loudness, before it's turned down. | −30 to +20 dB | 0 dB | −6, −3, 0, 3 |
| **Range** | The most the band is turned down. | 1 to 24 dB | 6 dB | 3, 6, 10 |

The de-esser never makes any frequency louder. Right at **Frequency** it takes about half the range, and it reaches the full range about an octave above.

It closes in 1 ms and lets go over 60 ms. You can't change those times.

## Read Status and Loudness

**Threshold** follows the clip's own loudness, the way the [Gate's](/audio/gate/#the-threshold-follows-the-clip) does, so a trim, a pan change or a different channel choice moves it. Two read-outs show what it means for this clip. With several clips selected, both read "—".

**Loudness** is the level the threshold is measured from, for example "−41.7 LUFS". It reads "measuring…" until the clip has been measured.

**Status** says where the de-esser acts, or why it isn't working:

| Status | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| off | **Reduce sibilance** isn't ticked. |
| Acts above −41.7 dBFS | The clip's loudness plus the **Threshold**. |
| Waits for its loudness | The clip hasn't been measured yet. |
| Not de-essing: too short | The clip plays for under 0.4 s, too short to measure. |
| Not de-essing: too quiet | The clip is too quiet to measure. |
| Not de-essing: no sound | The clip plays no sound in this timeline, or it's a nest clip. |

Until the clip's loudness is measured it plays without the de-esser, and an export waits. See [Before the clip's loudness is measured](/audio/gate/#before-the-clips-loudness-is-measured).

## Good to know

- The de-esser runs after the [gate](/audio/gate/) and the [leveller](/audio/leveller/), and before the [compressor](/audio/compressor/). See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).
- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, these controls write the action's end. The numbers glide across the action, and turning the de-esser on or off changes at the action's end.
- The de-esser does nothing on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.

## Related

- [Gate](/audio/gate/)
- [EQ](/audio/eq/)
- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/)
- [Compressor](/audio/compressor/)

---
title: "Match Audio"
description: "Give several clips the loudness and speech tone of one of them, so takes from different microphones or rooms sit together, in one undo step."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Match Audio makes selected clips sound like one of them, the reference. It sets each other clip's loudness and speech tone in one undo step, which helps when two takes came from different microphones or rooms.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Match Audio…"
  tools="match_audio"
  needs="Nothing. Speech detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## Match clips to a reference

<Steps>

1. Select the clips, including the one that already sounds right. You need at least two clips that could play sound. A nest clip or a clip with no sound doesn't count, and with fewer than two the menu item is dimmed.

2. Choose **Clip ▸ Match Audio…**.

3. In **Match to:**, choose the reference.

4. Leave **Loudness** and **EQ** ticked, or untick the one you don't want. **Match** is greyed out with both off.

5. Choose **Match**.

</Steps>

The Measuring Sound sheet stays up while each clip is measured as it plays, which takes a moment on a long clip. It counts "Clip 1 of 3…" as it goes. Nothing changes until every clip is measured, and **Cancel** leaves everything as it is.

When it finishes, the change is one undo step called "Match Audio". The results are ordinary settings in the [Volume](/audio/volume/), [Limiter](/audio/limiter/) and [EQ](/audio/eq/) sections, so you can adjust them afterwards.

The sheet opens with both boxes ticked and the first clip chosen every time. It doesn't remember your last choice.

## Choose the reference

**Match to:** lists the clips in timeline order, by start time and then by track, and the first is chosen. Each row reads `name — track — m:ss (clip id)`, for example `Interview — Video — 0:42 (clip 12)`, so you can tell two clips with the same name apart.

The reference itself isn't changed. Frame Job measures it once as it sounds in the timeline: through its own settings, its limiter and its volume, but without its fades, ducking or Mute. Its loudness at that point is the target for the other clips.

## What Loudness sets

**Loudness** runs [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode on each other clip, with the reference's loudness as the target. It sets the clip's volume, measured through the clip's settings as they'll be after the match. When the clip's peaks would pass −1 dBTP at that loudness, it also sets the clip's limiter at that ceiling.

A clip so quiet that it needs more than the volume's ceiling of 32× stops there and ends up quieter than the reference.

Loudness doesn't need speech, so you can use it on music by unticking **EQ**.

## What EQ sets

**EQ** gives each other clip the tone of the reference's voice. Frame Job compares the average spectrum of each clip's speech with the reference's, in 23 third-octave bands from 79 Hz to 12.7 kHz. Only speech counts: what the clip's sound analysis found, or the spans saved for [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/). A clip needs about a second of speech.

Each clip is measured with its EQ's shelves and bands off. The difference, less the overall level, is then fitted with the EQ's low shelf, three bands and high shelf:

- Each gain stays within ±12 dB.
- Each band's Q stays between 0.5 and 4.
- A band is only used where the difference is at least 0.5 dB.

Those five parts replace the clip's own. Its high-pass, low-pass and [hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/) stay as they were, and **Bypass** is turned off.

## What stays the same

Match Audio writes only volume, limiter and EQ. Every other section, the fades, ducking, pan and Mute are left alone.

Choosing **Match** again with the same choice changes nothing. Frame Job beeps and adds no undo step.

## When a clip can't be matched

A clip that can't be matched is skipped, and the others are still matched. No message names a skipped clip, so if one sounds unchanged, check it against the list below.

If the reference can't be used, or nothing can be matched, Frame Job beeps, changes nothing and puts the reason at the foot of the inspector. A reference's reason starts "The reference, clip 12,". When every clip fails, it starts "Nothing could be matched." and gives each clip's reason.

| The reason says | What it means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "is still being analysed — its loudness has not been measured yet" | Frame Job hasn't finished with the file, which often happens straight after an import. | Try again in a moment. |
| "is still being analysed — its speech has not been detected yet" | The same, for speech. This only applies with **EQ** on. | Try again in a moment, or untick **EQ**. |
| "plays no sound in this timeline" | Nothing from this clip reaches the mix. | Choose another clip. |
| "plays for under 0.4 s" | The clip is too short to have a loudness. | Choose a longer clip, or trim this one longer. |
| "is under −70 LUFS" | There's no sound to match. | Choose another clip. |
| "has under 1 s of speech" | The part that plays has too little speech to measure a tone. | Untick **EQ**, or choose a clip with more speech. |
| "has under 12 third-octave bands within 50 dB of its loudest" | The reference's sound is too narrow to match a tone to. | Choose another reference, or untick **EQ**. |
| "shares under 12 third-octave bands with the reference" | This clip and the reference have too little of the spectrum in common. | Untick **EQ** for this clip. |

If the project changes while the clips are being measured, nothing is applied. Frame Job beeps, and the foot of the inspector says "the project changed while its sound was being measured, so nothing changed. Choose Match Audio again."

## Good to know

- Match Audio matches the average tone of speech. It doesn't match the room, reverb, noise or dynamics. For those, see [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/), [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/) and the [Compressor](/audio/compressor/).
- You match to a clip, not to a track or a whole mix.
- Like Normalize, it writes each clip's own settings even when the playhead is inside an [action](/audio/animate-sound/).
- With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, it works on the clips inside the nest.

## With an agent

`match_audio` takes the reference and the clips directly, with no sheet. Unlike the menu, it answers with what happened to each clip, including each skipped clip and why. A nest can't be matched or used as the reference, and the call fails if Loudness and EQ are both off. See [Tools: audio](/mcp/tools-audio/).

## Related

- [Normalize](/audio/normalize/)
- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/)
- [EQ](/audio/eq/)
- [Limiter](/audio/limiter/)

---
title: "Voice Isolation"
description: "Keep the voice in a clip and remove background noise, music and room echo, using Apple's voice model on your Mac."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Voice Isolation keeps the voice in a clip and removes what's around it: background noise, music and the echo of the room. It uses Apple's on-device voice model, so nothing leaves your Mac.

<AtAGlance
  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Isolation"
  tools="set_audio"
  needs="Nothing. The voice model runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## Isolate a voice

<Steps>

1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **Voice Isolation** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).

2. Tick **Isolate voice**. The Amount goes to 80 % and **Status** reads "Rendering…".

3. Keep working. The clip plays without isolation until **Status** reads "Ready", then the editor switches over by itself.

4. Listen, and change **Amount** if you need to.

</Steps>

Isolation also reduces room echo, so there's no separate control for reverb.

## The controls

| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Isolate voice** | Turns isolation on at 80 %, or off. | On or off | Off |
| **Amount** | How much of the isolated voice replaces the clip's own sound. Quick values: 50, 80 and 100 %. | 0 to 100 % | 0 % (off) |
| **Status** | What the isolated voice is doing. See [What Status says](#what-status-says). | | Off |

Setting **Amount** above 0 also turns isolation on, and 0 turns it off. **Reset** in the section's header does the same as unticking the box.

## Choose an amount

Amount blends the isolated voice with the clip's own sound.

- **At 80 %**, the pauses between words drop by about 14 dB and keep a little of the room, so the voice doesn't sit in dead silence. This is what the box turns on.
- **At 100 %**, the pauses are silent.
- **Below that**, more of the original sound comes through.

Changing Amount takes effect at once. It doesn't need the isolated voice to be worked out again.

## While it renders

The isolated voice is worked out once for each clip, in the background, when you turn it on. Until it's ready the clip plays without it, and the editor switches over by itself.

Trimming or slipping the clip works it out again, because the clip then plays a different part of its file.

An export waits for every isolated clip to be ready, and its sheet reads "Preparing…" while it does, so a file is never written without isolation. If a clip's isolated voice can't be made, the export stops with "Clip 12's isolated voice could not be rendered:" and the reason.

## What Status says

| Status | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Off | Isolation is off for this clip. |
| Rendering… | The isolated voice is being worked out. The clip plays without it for now. |
| Ready | The clip plays with isolation. |
| Plays without it at this speed | The clip has a speed change, a ramp or a freeze frame. See below. |
| Waits for the reversed copy | The clip is reversed, and its reversed copy isn't ready yet. |
| Not rendered: and a reason | It failed, for example "Not rendered: its media cannot be found". |
| — | Several clips are selected. |

## Speed, ramps and freeze frames

Isolation plays only at normal speed. A clip with a [speed change](/speed/change-speed/), a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) or a [freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) plays without it, and **Status** says so.

A [reversed](/speed/reverse/) clip is isolated once its reversed copy is ready.

## Good to know

- Isolation comes first in the clip's sound, before the channel choice, the EQ, noise reduction and the compressor. You can use it with [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/), which then works on the isolated sound. A [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) is made from the isolated voice too. See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).
- Two clips cut from one take are isolated separately, so the sound at the join may differ slightly.
- Isolation does nothing on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip, and its **Status** reads "Off". Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, **Isolate voice** and **Amount** write the action's end, and the Amount glides across the action, from 0 when the clip's own Amount is 0. The isolated voice is still made for a clip whose own isolation is off.

## With an agent

`set_audio` sets the amount from 0 to 1. An agent can't read **Status**, because the render's state isn't in `get_project`, but an export still waits for it. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/).

## Related

- [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/)
- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/)
- [Voice effects](/audio/voice-effects/)
- [The Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/)

---
title: "Noise Reduction"
description: "Turn down steady background noise such as hiss, hum and fans, under speech as well as between words, with no noise sample needed."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Noise Reduction turns down steady background noise such as hiss, hum and fan noise. It works out the noise level from the clip itself, so you don't need to give it a sample of the noise or a stretch of silence.

<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Noise Reduction" tools="set_audio" />

## Remove noise

<Steps>

1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **Noise Reduction** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).

2. Raise **Remove noise** while you listen, until the noise is low enough and the voice still sounds natural.

</Steps>

| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Remove noise** | How much steady background noise to remove. Quick values: 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 %. | 0 to 100 % | 0 % (off) |
| **Depth** | Read-only. See [The Depth read-out](#the-depth-read-out). | | off |

**Reset** in the section's header sets **Remove noise** back to 0.

## The Depth read-out

**Depth** tells you the most any part of the sound can be turned down at this setting. It follows **Remove noise**:

| Remove noise | Depth reads |
| --- | --- |
| 0 % | off |
| 25 % | 2 dB at most |
| 50 % | 6 dB at most |
| 75 % | 12 dB at most |
| 100 % | floor removed |

Noise Reduction never removes more than the noise level it found, so a higher setting isn't a stronger cut across the whole sound.

## What it can't do

Noise Reduction isn't a gate. It works under speech as well as between words, and it doesn't silence the gaps. To turn the pauses down, use the [Gate](/audio/gate/).

It can't remove a sound that isn't steady, such as a door slam or a cough. A long held note may eventually be treated as noise.

To remove music or voices in the background, or the echo of a room, use [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/). The two work together: Noise Reduction then works on the isolated sound.

## Good to know

- It runs after the EQ and [hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/), and before the [Gate](/audio/gate/) and the [Compressor](/audio/compressor/). See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).
- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, **Remove noise** writes the action's end and the amount glides across the action.
- Noise Reduction set on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip has no effect. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.

## Related

- [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/)
- [Hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/)
- [Gate](/audio/gate/)
- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/)

---
title: "Hum removal"
description: "Notch out mains hum at 50 or 60 Hz and its harmonics, and leave the voice between them alone."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Hum removal cuts the low electrical hum that mains power can leave on a recording. It places a narrow notch at the mains frequency and at each of its multiples, and leaves the sound between the notches alone.

<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Hum" tools="set_audio" />

## Remove hum

<Steps>

1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **Hum** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).

2. Tick **Remove hum**. It starts at 60 Hz, 30 dB deep, with 4 harmonics.

3. Set **Mains** to the frequency where the recording was made.

4. If you can still hear the hum, raise **Depth** or **Harmonics**.

</Steps>

The other controls are dimmed until **Remove hum** is ticked. **Reset** in the section's header turns hum removal off.

## The controls

| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Remove hum** | Turns hum removal on. | On or off | Off |
| **Mains** | The mains frequency where the recording was made: 50 Hz in most of the world, 60 Hz in the Americas and parts of Asia. | 50 Hz or 60 Hz | 60 Hz |
| **Depth** | How far each notch turns the hum down. Quick values: 12, 24, 30 and 48 dB. | 6 to 60 dB | 30 dB |
| **Harmonics** | How many notches: the mains frequency and its multiples. Quick values: 1, 2, 4 and 8. | 1 to 8 | 4 |

At 60 Hz with 4 harmonics, the notches sit at 60, 120, 180 and 240 Hz.

Each notch is about a tenth of the mains frequency wide, whatever its depth, so a notch at 60 Hz is about 6 Hz wide.

## Good to know

- Hum removal runs after the [EQ](/audio/eq/). Its notches appear in the EQ section's drawn curve, but the EQ's **Bypass** doesn't turn them off.
- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, these controls write the action's end. **Depth** glides across the action. **Mains**, **Harmonics** and turning hum removal on or off change at the action's end, with no glide.
- Hum removal set on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip has no effect. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.

## Related

- [EQ](/audio/eq/)
- [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/)
- [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/)

---
title: "Gate"
description: "Turn a clip down in the pauses between phrases, so room noise and breaths get quieter while the speech stays as it is."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The gate turns a clip down in its pauses. When the sound falls below the threshold it's pushed further down, so room noise and breaths between phrases get quieter while the speech itself is untouched.

<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Gate" tools="set_audio" />

<Shot
  name="09c-clip-sound-dynamics.inspector"
  alt="The Gate section of the Sound tab with Gate pauses ticked: Threshold −10 dB, Ratio 4.0:1, Range 20 dB, Attack 1 ms, Hold 50 ms, Release 100 ms, Status reading Opens above −31.8 dBFS, and Loudness −21.8 LUFS."
/>

## Gate the pauses

<Steps>

1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **Gate** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).

2. Tick **Gate pauses**. It starts at the [defaults](#the-controls), which work from the clip's own loudness.

3. Play the clip. If the ends of words are being cut, raise **Hold** or lower **Threshold**.

4. If the pauses aren't quiet enough, raise **Range**. If they sound too empty, lower it.

</Steps>

The other controls are dimmed until **Gate pauses** is ticked. **Reset** in the section's header turns the gate off.

## The controls

| Control | What it does | Range | Default | Quick values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Threshold** | How far under the clip's loudness the gate opens. | −40 to 0 dB | −10 dB | −20, −15, −10, −6 |
| **Ratio** | How strongly sound under the threshold is turned down. At 4:1, each dB under the threshold becomes 3 dB further down. | 1:1 to 20:1 | 4:1 | 2, 4, 10, 20 |
| **Range** | The most the gate ever takes away. | 1 to 80 dB | 20 dB | 10, 20, 40, 80 |
| **Attack** | How quickly it opens when the sound rises. | 0 to 100 ms | 1 ms | 1, 5, 10 |
| **Hold** | How long it stays open after the sound falls, so the ends of words aren't clipped. | 0 to 500 ms | 50 ms | 0, 50, 100, 200 |
| **Release** | How quickly it closes after the hold. | 1 to 2,000 ms | 100 ms | 50, 100, 250, 500 |

## The threshold follows the clip

**Threshold** is set in dB under the clip's own loudness, not at a fixed level, so the same setting works on a quiet recording and a loud one. A trim, a pan change or a different channel choice moves the loudness, and the threshold moves with it.

That loudness is the Loudness figure in the [Volume](/audio/volume/) section. It's measured before noise reduction, the compressor, the volume, the fades and ducking, so moving the Volume slider doesn't change where the gate opens.

## Read Status and Loudness

Two read-outs at the foot of the section show what the threshold means for this clip. With several clips selected, both read "—".

**Loudness** is the level the threshold is measured from, for example "−21.8 LUFS". It reads "measuring…" until the clip has been measured.

**Status** says where the gate opens, or why it isn't working:

| Status | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| off | **Gate pauses** isn't ticked. |
| Opens above −31.8 dBFS | The clip's loudness plus the **Threshold**. Here, −21.8 LUFS with a −10 dB threshold. |
| Waits for its loudness | The clip hasn't been measured yet. See below. |
| Not gating: too short | The clip plays for under 0.4 s, too short to measure. |
| Not gating: too quiet | The clip is too quiet to measure. |
| Not gating: no sound | The clip plays no sound in this timeline, or it's a nest clip. |

## Before the clip's loudness is measured

The gate, the [leveller](/audio/leveller/) and the [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/) all depend on the clip's measured loudness. Until it lands, the clip plays without them, and the preview picks them up by itself.

An export waits until every gated, levelled or de-essed clip has been measured. After five minutes without a measurement it stops, saying that the clip's loudness or speech hasn't been measured yet, and to wait for the Status rows to show the clip's loudness and export again.

A clip that can't be measured, because it's under 0.4 s or too quiet, plays and exports without them, and the export doesn't wait for it.

## Good to know

- The gate runs after [noise reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/) and before the leveller, the de-esser and the [compressor](/audio/compressor/). See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).
- The gate doesn't look ahead, so a loud start after a long pause can lose its first millisecond while the gate opens.
- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, these controls write the action's end. The numbers glide across the action, and turning the gate on or off changes at the action's end.
- The gate does nothing on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.

## Related

- [Leveller](/audio/leveller/)
- [De-esser](/audio/de-esser/)
- [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/)
- [Compressor](/audio/compressor/)

---
title: "De-esser"
description: "Tame the hard s, sh and t sounds a close microphone exaggerates, turning down only the top of the voice while they last."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The de-esser tames sibilance, the hard "s", "sh" and "t" sounds a close microphone exaggerates. It listens to the sound above its frequency and turns only that band down while it's over the threshold, so the rest of the voice keeps its level.

<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ De-esser" tools="set_audio" />

## Reduce sibilance

<Steps>

1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **De-esser** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).

2. Tick **Reduce sibilance**. It starts at 6,000 Hz, a threshold of 0 dB and a range of 6 dB.

3. Play a part with hard "s" sounds. If they're still sharp, lower **Threshold** or raise **Range**.

4. If the voice sounds dull or lisped, raise **Threshold** or lower **Range**. Move **Frequency** to where the sibilance sits in this voice.

</Steps>

The other controls are dimmed until **Reduce sibilance** is ticked. **Reset** in the section's header turns the de-esser off.

## The controls

| Control | What it does | Range | Default | Quick values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Frequency** | Where the sibilant band starts. | 2,000 to 12,000 Hz | 6,000 Hz | 4,000, 5,000, 6,000, 8,000 |
| **Threshold** | How loud the band must get, relative to the clip's loudness, before it's turned down. | −30 to +20 dB | 0 dB | −6, −3, 0, 3 |
| **Range** | The most the band is turned down. | 1 to 24 dB | 6 dB | 3, 6, 10 |

The de-esser never makes any frequency louder. Right at **Frequency** it takes about half the range, and it reaches the full range about an octave above.

It closes in 1 ms and lets go over 60 ms. You can't change those times.

## Read Status and Loudness

**Threshold** follows the clip's own loudness, the way the [Gate's](/audio/gate/#the-threshold-follows-the-clip) does, so a trim, a pan change or a different channel choice moves it. Two read-outs show what it means for this clip. With several clips selected, both read "—".

**Loudness** is the level the threshold is measured from, for example "−41.7 LUFS". It reads "measuring…" until the clip has been measured.

**Status** says where the de-esser acts, or why it isn't working:

| Status | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| off | **Reduce sibilance** isn't ticked. |
| Acts above −41.7 dBFS | The clip's loudness plus the **Threshold**. |
| Waits for its loudness | The clip hasn't been measured yet. |
| Not de-essing: too short | The clip plays for under 0.4 s, too short to measure. |
| Not de-essing: too quiet | The clip is too quiet to measure. |
| Not de-essing: no sound | The clip plays no sound in this timeline, or it's a nest clip. |

Until the clip's loudness is measured it plays without the de-esser, and an export waits. See [Before the clip's loudness is measured](/audio/gate/#before-the-clips-loudness-is-measured).

## Good to know

- The de-esser runs after the [gate](/audio/gate/) and the [leveller](/audio/leveller/), and before the [compressor](/audio/compressor/). See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).
- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, these controls write the action's end. The numbers glide across the action, and turning the de-esser on or off changes at the action's end.
- The de-esser does nothing on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.

## Related

- [Gate](/audio/gate/)
- [EQ](/audio/eq/)
- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/)
- [Compressor](/audio/compressor/)
